correctness.rationale: For each generic objective-order permutation the exposed Minkowski-sum vertex is the sum of positive tube coefficients times their first coordinates. Swapping adjacent labels u,v only changes tubes containing both and disjoint from the prefix A; positivity makes the signed change a positive multiple of e_u−e_v, eliminating cancellation. In a tree every such tube contains the unique path R(u,v), and R itself is a tube. Hence survival iff all d−1 internal path vertices follow the contracted u-v adjacent block. Of the (n−1)! undirected u-v edges exactly 1/d satisfy this ordering, proving N=(n−1)!/d, valid all finite labelled trees n≥2 and all strictly positive real tube weights. Harary total and path/star asymptotics follow by pair-distance summation. Independently enumerated exposed vertices (not just an assumed path criterion) for small path/star trees and compared pair counts. Distinct surviving braid edges need not be distinct quotient polytope edges.

A researcher studying fan coarsening or adjacency statistics can use the exact distance-to-wall law.
